This is a '''list of telecommunications encryption terms'''. This list is derived in part from the ''Glossary of Telecommunication Terms'' published as [[Federal Standard 1037C]].
{{div col|colwidth=30em}}
*[[A5/1]]{{spaced ndash}}a [[stream cipher]] used to provide over-the-air communication [[privacy]] in the [[Global System for Mobile Communications|GSM]] [[Cell phone|cellular telephone]] standard.
*[[Bulk encryption]]
*[[Cellular Message Encryption Algorithm]]{{spaced ndash}}a block cipher which was used for securing mobile phones in the United States.
*[[Cipher]]
*[[Cipher device]]
*[[Cipher system]]
*[[Cipher text]]
*[[Ciphony]]<ref>{{Cite book |first=F. J. |last=Owens |title=Signal Processing of Speech |location=Houndmills |publisher=MacMillan Press |year=1993 |isbn=0-333-51922-1 }}</ref>
*Civision
*[[Codress message]]
<!--*[[compromise]]-->
*[[COMSEC equipment]]
<!--*[[cover]]-->
*[[Cryptanalysis]]
*[[Cryptographic key]]
*[[International Cryptology Conference|CRYPTO]] (International Cryptology Conference)
*[[Crypto phone]]
*[[Crypto-shredding]]
*[[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES) <ref>[[Don Coppersmith|Coppersmith, Don]]. (1994). [https://web.archive.org/web/20070615132907/http://www.research.ibm.com/journal/rd/383/coppersmith.pdf The data encryption standard (DES) and its strength against attacks]. ''IBM Journal of Research and Development'', '''38'''(3), 243–250.</ref>
*[[Decipher]]
*[[Code|Decode]]
*[[Decrypt]]
*[[DECT Standard Cipher]]
*[[Descrambler]]
*[[Dncipher]]
*[[Code|Encode]]
*[[Encoding law]]
*[[Encrypt]]
*[[End-to-end encryption]]
<!--*[[garble]]-->
*[[Group (mathematics)|group]]
*[[IMSI-catcher]]{{spaced ndash}}an eavesdropping device used for interception of cellular phones and usually is undetectable for users of mobile phones.
*[[Key distribution center]] (KDC)
*[[Key management]]
*[[Key stream]]
*[[KSD-64]]
*[[Link encryption]]
*[[MISTY1]]
*[[Multiplex link encryption]]
*[[Net control station]] (NCS)
*[[Null cipher]]
*[[One-time pad]]
*[[Over the Air Rekeying]] (OTAR)
*[[Plaintext]]
*[[PPPoX]]
*[[Protected distribution system]] (PDS)
*[[Protection interval]] (PI)
*[[Pseudorandom number generator]]
*[[Public-key cryptography]]
*[[RED/BLACK concept]]
*[[RED signal]]
<!--*[[rekeying]]-->
*[[Remote rekeying]]
*[[Security management]]
*[[Spoofing attack|Spoofing]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Schneier|first=Bruce|title=Caller ID Spoofing|url=http://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2006/03/caller_id_spoof.html|publisher=schneier.com|access-date=16 January 2011|date=3 March 2006}}</ref>
*Squirt{{spaced ndash}}to load or transfer code key from an electronic key storage device. See [[Over the Air Rekeying]].
*[[STU-III]]{{spaced ndash}}a family of secure telephones introduced in 1987 by the [[National Security Agency]] for use by the United States government, its contractors, and its allies.
*[[Superencryption]]
*[[Synchronous crypto-operation]]
*[[Transmission security key]] (TSK)
*[[Trunk encryption device]] (TED)
*[[NSA product types|Types 1, 2, 3, and 4 encryption]]
*[[Unique key]]
<!--*[[variant]]-->
<!--*[[vocoder]]-->
*[[VoIP VPN]]{{spaced ndash}}combines voice over IP and [[virtual private network]] technologies to offer a method for delivering [[secure voice]].
*[[ZRTP]]{{spaced ndash}}a cryptographic key-agreement protocol used in  [[Voice over Internet Protocol]] (VoIP) phone telephony.<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-zimmermann-avt-zrtp
